rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The frog's cardiovascular and respiratory systems show the amphibian compromise. A three-chambered heart — two atria and a single ventricle with a spiral-valved conus — drives incomplete double circulation: pulmocutaneous arches send blood to lungs and skin, systemic arches to the body, with some mixing in the single ventricle.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Body to sinus venosus to right atrium. Lungs to pulmonary vein to left atrium. Both to the ventricle. Ventricle to truncus.
Three arches on each side: carotid, systemic, pulmocutaneous.
Inspiration: nostrils open, floor down, then nostrils shut, floor up, air into lungs.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The ventricle is single. Two atria do not make a four-chambered heart. The chambers that count are two atria plus one ventricle.  ·  Oxygenated blood from the skin enters the right atrium, via the sinus venosus. Only pulmonary blood enters the left atrium.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not draw four chambers. The spiral valve is inside the truncus, not a wall that divides the ventricle into two.  ·  Hibernation uses skin. Do not write that a hibernating frog breathes with lungs at the summer rate.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Cutaneous respiration*** — the moist vascular skin exchanges gases in water and at rest.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Digestive organs are the previous note. The reproductive system of the frog is not this topic.  ·  Arch names are limited to carotid, systemic and pulmocutaneous.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Write the heart route as eight arrows on one line.  ·  Write inspiration as four actions: glottis, nostrils, floor, then the switch.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Skin, mouth, lungs — three ways to breathe."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Why is frog circulation called incomplete double circulation? **Answer.** **Double** because blood passes through the heart **twice per complete circuit** — once to the lungs/skin (pulmocutaneous arch) and once to the body (systemic arches).…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Incomplete double circulation:** one ventricle mixes oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, yet the spiral valve and timing keep enough separation for a poikilotherm's low metabolism.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Heart: two atria + single ventricle; sinus venosus → right atrium; pulmonary veins → left atrium; conus arteriosus with spiral valve; incomplete double circulation (pulmocutaneous + systemic arches); hepatic and renal portal systems.  ·  Respiration: cutaneous (skin — dominant in water), buccopharyngeal (buccal lining, at rest), pulmonary (simple sac lungs, during activity).  ·  Pulmonary breathing: buccal floor lowers, air in via nostrils → nostrils close, glottis opens, floor rises → air forced into lungs; expiration by elastic recoil.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: In water, the frog obtains most of its oxygen through the skin — a frog can survive long dives without surfacing.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The truncus arteriosus is part of the arterial exit. It is not a vein, and it is not a fourth chamber.  ·  Adult frogs do not breathe with gills. Gills are larval. Hibernating adults rely on skin.  ·  The respiratory-system question repeated at 5m in 2022 and 2024 — the three surfaces plus the breathing mechanism is the full answer.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: "A three-chambered heart is a compromise between fish and mammal."  ·  Why can a frog survive long dives without surfacing? **Answer.** Because it carries a **backup breathing surface**: the skin.
